summary_paraphrase: A village goat chasing the metal rooster on a church gets stuck on its roof; one neighbour after another offers a better idea to bring him down, and he eats each one until the carpenter's ramp lets him slide to the girl who owns him, and the whole crowd tells her not to let him out again.

beats.function: why he climbed; the hen/rooster joke
hug and a question to the reader
the whole cast answers in chorus

characters.name: Rocky
characters.desire: to eat whatever is in reach
characters.change: none; he is the same goat at the end

humor_notes: Animal-behaviour comedy: the goat eats each rescue; a hen/rooster/not-a-real-rooster correction; the closing chorus turns the opening complaint into a rule.

repetition.description: 'but Rocky wanted to eat the …' followed by a neighbour offering a better idea
repetition.why: the listener can predict that each new idea will be eaten, and the pattern breaks when the ramp works

repetition.description: 'I have an idea' / 'I have a better idea' spoken by three helpers in turn
repetition.why: a short sayable line that marks each new attempt

repetition.description: the opening complaint about who let the goat out returns as the cast's closing chorus; p10 lists every helper
repetition.why: closes the circle and recaps the cast for the reader

notes: Two of the three rescue ideas (the box tower, the plank ramp) are shown only in the pictures; the text names who has an idea but not what it is.
The weathercock the goat was chasing is in the picture from p2, before the text names it.
The climax page carries one shouted line; the picture shows the ramp being raised.

strengths: a clear try-fail-try pattern with a sayable line on each attempt
the final question to the reader is answered on the last page by the whole cast
comic animal behaviour carries the tension without real danger
weaknesses: six named adults in eleven pages; only the recap on p10 helps the reader keep them apart
the child owner only begs and shouts; adults solve the problem
as text alone the rescue ideas are not explained (they live in the pictures)

anti_patterns.note: four named neighbours plus parents and the child for a 5-6 listener; the cumulative recap softens it
the carpenter's ramp brings the child's goat down; Rose has no idea of her own

child_appeal_heuristic.label: Research heuristic — not validated
child_appeal_heuristic.rationale: Scores are the analyst's reading of the pages, not observations of children.

age_suitability.notes: Mild comic peril at the climax (research 4/5, about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale); adults stand on a car roof and the goat slides down a plank — a model for MagicPaper would keep the try-fail pattern and give the child the winning idea.

metrics.lexicon_note: direct_address and sound_words are lexicon counts: a floor, not a measure. direct_address counts second-person words anywhere, dialogue included — it is not narrator-to-reader address

repetition.end_rhyme_note: heuristic: consecutive lines sharing a final two letters
